home.title: Matthew Hua

home.methodTitle: One person. An entirely personal approach.
home.methodCopy: Touch, breath, temperature, attention and movement come together around you. The starting point is how you feel. The session takes shape from there.
home.practiceCopy: An unhurried encounter in Zurich, shaped around the person behind the responsibilities.
home.aboutTitle: A life across borders. A practice without a script.

method.title: Six elements. One practice.
method.intro: A connected approach to how you feel, move and meet the moment. Each element has its place. Your session brings together what is relevant to you.

elements.name: Mindset
elements.line: What we notice shapes what we experience.
elements.copy: An invitation to explore attention, perspective and the way we respond. Begin with a small experiment.

elements.name: Hot / Cold
elements.copy: Guided temperature experiences bring attention into the present. Preparation, individual suitability and a steady presence shape the work.

elements.name: Breathwork
elements.copy: A guided exploration of breathing and awareness, informed by Matthew's Wim Hof Method and Oxygen Advantage instructor training.

elements.name: Body
elements.copy: Classical, Thai, Chinese, Balinese, Shiatsu and sports influences meet a dynamic, personal style of bodywork. Contact and movement respond to the person on the table.

elements.name: Movement
elements.line: An active relationship with your body.
elements.copy: Supported movement, mobility and a curiosity about everyday physical experience. Explore how you move and where there is room for ease.

elements.name: Community
elements.line: Practice is something we can share.
elements.copy: Workshops and shared experiences create space to learn alongside others. Matthew brings a background in community health to the way he teaches and connects.

method.technologyIntro: Technology extends the repertoire. Matthew remains present, choosing and guiding the work in response to you.
method.releaseLine: The hands remain at the centre.
method.releaseCopy: Electrical stimulation is delivered through practitioner-worn coupling gloves. This equipment-assisted approach keeps touch and the practitioner's attention part of the session.
method.zimmerCopy: The Soleo family brings ultrasound and electrotherapy into a supervised session. The choice of application and settings depends on the equipment configuration and the individual.
handsItems: A personal rhythm of touch and movement
method.techNote: The approach and use of equipment are discussed individually before a session.

game.title: An experiment in attention.
game.intro: What you look for shapes what you remember.
game.introSub: A short memory experiment. Then a moment to reflect.
game.memorizeSub: You will be asked to find them from memory.
game.recall: Where were the three blue signals?
game.recallSub: Choose three positions. Take your time.
game.red: And where was the red signal?
game.redSub: Choose a quarter of the field, or say you are not sure.
game.revealCopy: The blue signals held your attention. The red signal was in the bottom-right quarter.
game.score: You remembered {count} of the 3 blue positions.
game.focusCopy: What we look for becomes easier to notice. This is an invitation to reflect, not a measure of your ability.
game.lessonCopy: When we keep counting problems, they can fill the picture. Support, small wins and reasons for gratitude may still be there, waiting to be noticed.
game.integrationTitle: Make room for a different signal.
game.integrationCopy: Through breath, touch, warmth, movement and presence, Matthew invites a different quality of attention to the body.
game.finalCopy: Tony Robbins has been a long-standing influence on Matthew's interest in personal development. Their meeting is part of a much longer journey of learning and practice.

practice.title: Space for the person behind it all.
practice.intro: Your work, your responsibilities, your pace of life. Here, the attention returns to you.

principles.title: Personal attention
principles.copy: Start with a conversation about how you feel and what brings you here. The session is shaped around that encounter.

principles.title: Discretion
principles.copy: A thoughtful, private setting for high-profile individuals, entrepreneurs and professionals who value a personal approach.

principles.title: An integrated practice
principles.copy: Bodywork, breath, mindset, movement and selected technology can come together within one considered session.

practice.processTitle: A conversation. A session. Room to reflect.

steps.title: Connect
steps.copy: Contact Matthew directly to discuss your interests, availability and any questions before booking.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.copy: At the studio near Sihlcity, take a moment to settle. Talk through the focus and agree on the approach together.

faqs.q: How do I arrange a session?
faqs.a: Email info@healwell.ch or contact Matthew on WhatsApp at +41 76 506 74 88. Availability, session length and fees are agreed directly.
Matthew is EMR-registered for five methods. Reimbursement depends on your supplementary insurance, the method and your policy. Please check coverage with your insurer before booking.

faqs.q: Where does the session take place?
faqs.a: The Healwell studio is at Rüdigerstrasse 7, Ground Floor, 8045 Zürich, near Sihlcity. The Contact page includes directions.

faqs.q: Which language can we use in a session?
faqs.a: English and German are working languages; Matthew also has some Mandarin. The website is available in ten languages. Please discuss your preferred session language when enquiring.

about.title: A life in motion.
about.intro: Born in Vietnam. Raised in Australia. Practising in Zurich. A life of learning, service and hands-on craft.

chapters.label: 01 / Between shores
chapters.title: A wider way of seeing.
chapters.copy: Matthew left Vietnam by boat with his family and arrived in Australia as a child. In Sydney, meditation entered his life during his teenage years. Community health work and studies in Social Science and International Studies at the University of Technology Sydney followed.

chapters.label: 02 / The language of touch
chapters.title: Learning, through the hands.
chapters.copy: His massage learning began in Sydney in 1997 and continued in Guangzhou and Zurich. Classical, Chinese, Balinese, Thai, Shiatsu and sports influences became part of a dynamic personal style. Healwell gave that practice a home in Zurich.

chapters.label: 03 / Beyond the familiar
chapters.title: The teacher keeps practising.
chapters.copy: An Advanced Wim Hof Method Instructor and Oxygen Advantage Breathwork Instructor, Matthew continues to explore the practices he teaches. His experiences include a winter hike with Wim Hof, workshop assistance in Sweden and a barefoot Zurich marathon.

chapters.label: 04 / Passing it on
chapters.title: From the table to the international floor.
chapters.copy: Competition brought Swiss freestyle gold, Eastern Freestyle gold in Germany and European gold in Asian Inspired / Nuad Thai in Rome. By 2026, his international work included the European Feedback Jury near Paris and a judging appointment in Tokyo.

timeline.text: Healwell is established in Zurich; its public brand story begins in 2018.
EMR registration for five recognised methods.
Swiss freestyle gold; gold and silver at the Universal Massage Championship in Germany.
European category gold in Rome; involvement in Zurich's VAULT studio.
International judging, feedback and practitioner mentoring.

about.foundationCopy: His EMR-recognised methods are Therapeutic Massage, Classical Massage, Foot Reflexology, Manual Lymphatic Drainage and Autogenic Training. Continued learning and international exchange sit alongside that foundation.
about.tonyCopy: Tony Robbins has influenced Matthew's interest in personal development for more than 35 years. Their meeting belongs to a continuing exploration of attention, personal responsibility and how we meet experience.
about.todayTitle: Rooted in Zurich. Open to the world.
about.todayCopy: Alongside Healwell, Matthew's work connects with VAULT in Zurich. Teaching, collaborative practice and international exchanges continue to bring new perspectives back to the studio.
